sections.h2: What are a Cortlandt seller's choices, and when does cash make sense?
sections.html:
Selling in Cortlandt means weighing an agent listing against a private sale or a cash purchase of the house as-is. Cash tends to make sense when the property needs work, the owner is behind on payments or taxes, an estate must be wrapped up, or a closing date cannot slip.

A listing can stall while a seller pays for repairs before the first showing. A cash buyer accepts the house with its flaws and quotes accordingly, which is why the offer comes in below a polished listing. Put both numbers beside the payoff on your mortgage, any unpaid tax and the costs you would pay at closing.

  • An agent listing suits a house that shows well with time to wait.
  • A direct sale to someone you know suits owners who are comfortable with contracts.
  • A cash sale suits a home with deferred maintenance, an inheritance, a tenant dispute or a looming tax penalty.

sections.h2: Where is Cortlandt, and how does its geography affect a house?
sections.html:
Cortlandt sits in the northwestern corner of Westchester County. The Hudson River and the City of Peekskill bound it on the west, Putnam County's Philipstown and Putnam Valley on the north, Yorktown on the east and New Castle and Ossining on the south. The town was incorporated in 1788, covers 50 square miles in all and holds nearly 11 square miles of water, about a fifth of its area.

It contains the incorporated villages of Buchanan and Croton-on-Hudson and hamlets including Cortlandt Manor, Montrose, Crugers and Verplanck, along with neighborhoods such as Mount Airy, Oscawana and Van Cortlandtville. US Route 9 follows the river, the eastern end of the Bear Mountain Bridge lands here, and Metro-North serves the Cortlandt and Croton-Harmon stations, with Amtrak also stopping at Croton-Harmon. In 1781 George Washington's army crossed the Hudson at King's Ferry, between Verplanck's Point and Stony Point.

The Census Bureau counted 42,545 residents in 2020 and estimates 42,413 for July 1, 2025.

sections.h2: Which school districts and village lines apply to a Cortlandt address?
sections.html:
The Tax Receiver collects for five school districts: Croton-Harmon, Hendrick Hudson, Lakeland, Putnam Valley and Yorktown. A Cortlandt address can therefore mean very different school taxes for houses a few miles apart. Name the district in any listing or offer packet, because buyers sort by it.

Village boundaries add another layer. The villages of Buchanan and Croton-on-Hudson levy their own village taxes, and those are billed separately from the Town and County bill. If you sell a house inside a village, ask the village office for its bill and its collection dates as well. The Tax Receiver's office page links to both villages for that purpose.

sections.h2: When do Cortlandt tax bills fall due, and what are the penalties?
sections.html:
Westchester towns act as collection agents, so the Cortlandt Tax Receiver bills Town, County and school taxes. The Town and County bill goes out by April 1 and is due April 30. The school bill goes out by September 1 and can be paid in full by September 30 or in two halves, the first by September 30 and the second by January 31.

  • Town and County penalty: 2% in May, 5% in June and July, 7% in August and September, 10% from October to December and 12% from January to April.
  • School first half: 2% in October, 5% in November, 7% in December and January, 10% in February and March, 12% in April.
  • Penalties cannot be waived by any Town employee.
  • Prior-year taxes unpaid by June 30 become a lien on July 1, and a property with taxes unpaid after 21 months can be foreclosed.

The office bills over 15,000 parcels and collects more than $188 million a year. It is at 1 Heady Street in Cortlandt Manor, open weekdays from 8:30 a.m. to 4 p.m. and on the last Saturday of April and September from 9 a.m. to noon. A drop box in the courtyard takes after-hours payments, no cash. Online payment adds a $1.00 fee for e-check or a 1.81% third-party fee for cards. Mail payments need a United States postmark on or before the due date, since postage meter marks do not count.

sections.h2: How do assessments, exemptions and grievances work in Cortlandt?
sections.html:
Cortlandt runs on a different calendar than most upstate towns. May 1 is tax status day, which is also the exemption and tax map change deadline. The tentative roll is published June 1, Grievance Day is the third Tuesday in June, and the final roll appears September 15. This year's Grievance Day was June 16, 2026. The 2027 date is Tuesday, June 15.

The Assessor's office says the prior year's final roll sets the current year's taxes, so the 2022 roll was used to print the 2023 to 2024 bills. A grievance is a challenge to the assessment, not the tax itself, and the Town suggests you ask whether you could actually sell for the full market value shown. Form RP-524 must be filed with the Assessment Office even if you plan to appear before the Board, and a mailed copy must arrive by 8 p.m. on Grievance Day.

Senior citizen and disability with limited income exemptions renew every year: the Assessor mails renewal forms in February and wants them back with supporting papers by May 1. If you are selling a house that carries one of these exemptions, tell the buyer that the benefit belongs to the owner and has to be applied for again after the sale.

Three recent changes are worth noting. Enhanced STAR no longer has an application, because the state verifies income yearly. The Town took over the Village of Croton's assessing function after the village gave it up in 2025. And a new exemption for veterans with a permanent and total disability rating needs local adoption: the Town scheduled a public hearing for November 17, 2026, the county and Croton had already adopted it, and the filing deadline would be May 1, 2027.

sections.h2: What do deeds and state transfer taxes look like for a Cortlandt sale?
sections.html:
Westchester County Clerk's Land Records Division records deeds, mortgages and satisfactions, and it takes electronic filings. Cover pages, Form TP-584 transfer tax returns and RP-5217 reports must be created through the clerk's PREP portal. Deeds go back to 1680 in its online search.

State transfer tax is $2 for each $500 of consideration, ordinarily paid by the seller, with the return and payment due no later than 15 days after the deed is delivered. On a price of $1 million or more, a separate 1% additional tax applies to the buyer. For permits and any open violations, start with the Town and, for village addresses, the village hall.

faqs.q: Does a Cortlandt house need repairs before it can be sold for cash?
faqs.a: No. A cash buyer takes the property as-is and prices in the work. Expect the offer to be lower than a repaired listing, and check for open permits or violations first.

faqs.q: When is the next Grievance Day in Cortlandt?
faqs.a: Tuesday, June 15, 2027. Grievance Day is the third Tuesday in June, and 2026's date, June 16, has passed. Exemption applications are due May 1.

faqs.q: Who collects property taxes in Cortlandt?
faqs.a: The Cortlandt Tax Receiver collects Town, County and school taxes at 1 Heady Street. Buchanan and Croton-on-Hudson bill their own village taxes separately.

faqs.q: What happens if I miss the April 30 Town and County tax date?
faqs.a: A 2% penalty applies in May, rising to 5% in June and July. The Town cannot waive it, so pay as soon as you can.

faqs.q: Where is a Cortlandt deed recorded?
faqs.a: At the Westchester County Clerk's Land Records Division in White Plains. File Form TP-584 with it, and build the cover page in the clerk's PREP portal.
